article.title: UN: Large-scale return of Afghan refugees strains Afghan economy
paras: Editor's note: this story was translated from the original VOA Dari article.
The return of millions of Afghan refugees from Iran and Pakistan has put pressure on the Afghan economy, according to the United Nations.
The United Nations Development Program in Afghanistan said Tuesday in a post on X that the large-scale return of Afghans has added “pressure on jobs, essential services and infrastructure.”
The U.N. said that nearly 1.3 million Afghans have returned, including those deported, from Pakistan and Iran, the two countries hosting most of Afghan refugees, to Afghanistan, so far in 2026.
UNDP adds that between 2023 and 2025, about 4.9 million Afghans returned to the country.

Even with the millions of returns, the U.N. says that 4.4 million Afghans are still living in Iran, including 1.4 million undocumented Afghans. About 1.6 million Afghans live in Pakistan including an estimated 159 thousand undocumented Afghans.
The U.N. said that “policy changes and economic pressures” in host countries have led to large-scale deportations and returns of Afghans.
The returns have further burdened vulnerable communities and essential services, according to the U.N.
The World Food Program said about 19.2 million people face acute food insecurity, while 4 million women and children are expected to suffer from malnutrition in 2027.

Afghan returnees are “with few or no resources, leaving them to settle in remote mountainous areas far from major roads and essential services. They live in makeshift shelters, often just tents under the scorching sun or on bare stones, with no access to clean water, food, or even basic shelter,” said the UNHCR. “Healthcare is out of reach, and many lack even the simplest identification documents, leaving them vulnerable and invisible in the margins of society.

Mohammad Bashir Doodyal, a former economics professor at Kabul University, told VOA that poverty, a lack of job opportunities and presence of diseases could pose major challenges to the integration of returnees into Afghan society.
“It is the responsibility of governments to plan ... to address these issues,” said Doodyal, adding that “it looks there are no such plans in place.”
He added that Afghanistan would need to improve its relations with neighboring countries and the international community to attract domestic and foreign investment needed to strengthen the economy.
“Afghanistan must emerge from isolation and have a government that the international community can trust and work with,” Doodyal said.

Khan Jan Alokozay, president of the Afghan chapter of the Pakistan-Afghanistan Joint Chamber of Commerce and Industry, told VOA that neither the government nor the private sector has the capacity to absorb millions of Afghans at once.
zh: 聯合國：阿富汗難民的大規模返國給阿富汗經濟帶來壓力
編者註：本文翻譯自美國之音（VOA）達里語原文報導。
據聯合國表示，數百萬阿富汗難民從伊朗和巴基斯坦返國，已對阿富汗經濟造成壓力。
聯合國開發計畫署駐阿富汗辦事處週二在 X 平台上發文表示，阿富汗人大規模返國已對「就業、基本服務及基礎設施」造成額外壓力。
聯合國表示，截至2026年，已有近130萬名阿富汗人從巴基斯坦和伊朗——這兩國收容了絕大多數阿富汗難民——返回阿富汗，其中包括被遣返者。
聯合國開發計畫署（UNDP）補充指出，在2023年至2025年間，約有490萬名阿富汗人返回該國。
儘管已有數百萬人返國，聯合國表示仍有440萬阿富汗人居住在伊朗，其中包括140萬無證阿富汗人。約有160萬阿富汗人居住在巴基斯坦，其中估計有15.9萬名無證阿富汗人。
聯合國表示，收容國的「政策變動與經濟壓力」導致阿富汗人遭到大規模驅逐出境及遣返。
據聯合國表示，這些返鄉潮進一步加重了弱勢群體及基本服務的負擔。
世界糧食計畫署表示，約有1,920萬人面臨嚴重的糧食不安全問題，而預計在2027年將有400萬名婦女和兒童遭受營養不良之苦。
聯合國難民署表示，阿富汗返鄉者「資源匱乏或根本沒有資源，迫使他們定居在遠離主要道路和基本服務的偏遠山區。他們住在臨時庇護所，往往只是在烈日下或光禿禿的石頭上搭起的帳篷，無法獲得乾淨的水、食物，甚至連基本的庇護所都沒有。」 「醫療保健遙不可及，許多人甚至連最簡單的身份證明文件都沒有，使他們處於社會邊緣，既脆弱又隱形。」
喀布爾大學前經濟學教授穆罕默德·巴希爾·杜迪亞爾向美國之音表示，貧困、就業機會匱乏以及疾病肆虐，都可能對歸國者融入阿富汗社會構成重大挑戰。
「政府有責任制定計畫……以解決這些問題，」杜迪亞爾表示，並補充道：「看來目前似乎並未制定此類計畫。」
他補充說，阿富汗需要改善與鄰國及國際社會的關係，以吸引強化經濟所需的國內外投資。
「阿富汗必須擺脫孤立狀態，並建立一個國際社會能夠信任且願意與之合作的政府，」杜迪亞爾表示。
巴基斯坦-阿富汗聯合工商會阿富汗分會會長汗·詹·阿洛科扎伊向美國之音表示，無論是政府還是私營部門，都無力一次性接納數百萬阿富汗人。
